name: BystanderEffect
initial_prompt: Create a collaborative philosophical discussion with alternating turns where users discuss philosophical statements referencing todays day and age.

variations.context: The ethics of the bystander effect

setting.relationship_dynamic: Friends discussing responsibility in everyday emergencies
setting.background: They discuss famous cases associated with the bystander effect and consider what an ordinary person should do when others are present
setting.conversation_style: Real-life ethical discussion with personal thought experiments

scenario_template.topic: Who is responsible when everyone assumes someone else will help?
scenario_template.note: They discuss a hypothetical emergency occurring in a crowded public place

scenario_template.topic: A person collapsing on a train platform
scenario_template.note: They imagine several people witnessing the incident without immediately intervening
One argues that every witness has a duty to act while the other emphasizes uncertainty and personal limitations
They ask how philosophers might determine when helping becomes a genuine moral obligation
They consider whether the obligation changes when intervention could put the helper in danger
They distinguish between being morally blameworthy, morally admirable, and legally obligated
They consider whether their standards for themselves should be different from their standards for other people

user1.name: User1
user1.role: Person who is genuinely curious about philosophical questions but may have strong intuitions, personal assumptions, or uncertainty about abstract concepts. They explore ideas through questions, examples, and personal reflections and may change their position when presented with convincing reasoning

user2.name: User2
user2.role: Person who is analytical and detail-oriented, enjoys examining arguments from multiple perspectives, and often challenges assumptions or asks for clarification. They are willing to reconsider their views but prefer careful reasoning and consistency before accepting a conclusion

assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.role: Philosophical discussion facilitator who helps users explore complex questions by clarifying concepts, identifying assumptions, presenting competing arguments and perspectives, asking thought-provoking questions, and distinguishing between claims, evidence, intuitions, and interpretations without forcing a definitive conclusion
